papers.title: Which Ellipses Are Outlines of a Given Ellipsoid? A Ratio Test with Unknown Focal Length
papers.abstract: When is an image ellipse the outline of a given ellipsoid with semi-axes $a <= b <= c? For a camera with square pixels, zero skew and known principal point, we show that it is an outline at focal length $f$ exactly when a cone ratio kappa(f), computed from two eigenvalues, is at most a/c; the middle semi-axis b plays no role. With f unknown, the admissible focal lengths form an interval; whether it is empty is decided by the smallest cone ratio over $f$, which, when attained, is obtained from an explicit quartic. The interval is bounded above only when the principal point is closer to the long axis of the ellipse than to its short axis. Thus one ellipse can rule out ellipsoids that are too round, never ones that are too elongated, and none if the principal point is unknown. Simulations and 45 Cassini images of Saturn's moons support the test.

papers.title: Hadwiger\'s Covering Conjecture in Three Dimensions
papers.abstract: Let $K \subset \R^3$ be an arbitrary convex body, that is, a compact convex subset of $\R^3$ with nonempty interior. We prove unconditionally that $K$ can be covered by eight smaller positive homothetic copies of itself: there exist a scalar $\lambda \in (0, 1)$ and translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_8 \in \R^3$ such that \[ K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{8} (\lambda K + v_i). \] This resolves Hadwiger's covering conjecture in three dimensions. The proof works in Boltyanski's equivalent boundary illumination formulation and is completely self-contained. Parallelepipeds are covered directly by eight translates of $\frac{2}{3} K$. For any convex body $K$ that is not a parallelepiped, we place its centrally symmetric halved difference body $S = \frac{1}{2}(K - K)$ in John's position ($B^3 \subseteq S$) and show that the spherical average of its support function satisfies $8 \int_{S^2} h_S \, d\sigmatilde < 12$, with equality only for orthogonal cubes. Using outer polyhedral approximations together with Cauchy's planar perimeter formula, the full spherical measure of directions not parallel to any boundary segment of $K$, and lower semicontinuity of curve variation, we find a unit vector $w_* \in S^2$ whose shadow boundary $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ on $K$ itself is a continuous closed curve of $S$-length strictly less than $12$. Splitting $\Shad{K}{w_*}$ into six contiguous arcs of $S$-length strictly less than $2$ and applying Helly's theorem in $\R^3$ illuminates each arc with one direction, while $\pm w_*$ illuminate the remainder of $\partial K$. The proof was discovered using an experimental harness on top of Gemini~4 Carbon and formally verified in Lean~4.

papers.title: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
papers.abstract: Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math. Nachr. 299 (2026): 2566--2589] cannot be omitted. We then give a novel spectral characterization of heat kernel upper bounds in terms of the first Dirichlet eigenpair of balls. In particular, on an unbounded proper geodesic Dirichlet space with volume doubling, reverse volume doubling and a scale-$r^\beta$ Poincar\'e inequality, the heat kernel upper estimate is equivalent to $\lambda(B(x,r))\asymp r^{-\beta}$ and a uniform comparison between the supremum of a nonnegative first eigenfunction and its value at $x$. Under elliptic Harnack inequality, we also prove that the mean exit-time scale on balls is equivalent to the scale on the bottom of the spectrum on balls. This proves Conjecture~4.15 of Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau. The Euclidean planar example given above also disproves the eigenvalue version of their Conjecture~4.16 on a characterization of the parabolic harnack inequality. We end by showing that our spectral conditions gives the correct characterization.

papers.title: On unique realisations of graphs under symmetry constraints
papers.abstract: Global rigidity asks whether a realisation of a graph is uniquely determined, up to Euclidean congruence, by its edge lengths. In this paper, we study global rigidity of bar-joint frameworks under finite point-group symmetry constraints. A framework is called forced-symmetric globally rigid in $d$-space if every realisation of the graph in $\mathbb R^d$ with the same edge lengths and the same prescribed symmetry is congruent to it. We establish symmetric extensions of two fundamental results on global rigidity. Our first result extends Hendrickson's necessary condition to the forced-symmetric setting. For symmetry-generic frameworks with an arbitrary finite point group acting freely on the vertices and with at least $d+2$ vertex orbits, we prove that forced-symmetric global rigidity implies forced-symmetric redundant rigidity. Our second result extends the classical characterisation of generic global rigidity for body-bar frameworks due to Connelly, Jord\'an and Whiteley. For the symmetric body-bar model considered here, we show that forced-symmetric global rigidity is a generic property and obtain a combinatorial characterisation in every dimension.

papers.title: An intrinsic criterion for Pansu differentials to be homomorphisms of nilpotent Lie groups
papers.abstract: By Pansu's theorem, Lipschitz maps between Carnot groups are differentiable almost everywhere, and their differentials are group homomorphisms. When the domain is instead a nilpotent Lie group with a bracket-generating left-invariant distribution, the Pansu differential is a homomorphism of an osculating Carnot group, which depends on an auxiliary choice of grading, and it need not be a homomorphism of the original group. We give an intrinsic criterion for when it is one, for a suitable choice of grading: the differential must vanish on an ideal that depends only on the group and its distribution, and comes from a universal quotient onto a Carnot group. The criterion holds automatically when the step of the target is small enough, and an explicit example shows that this threshold is sharp. Along the way, we determine exactly how the obstruction depends on the choice of grading.

papers.title: Linear programming certificates for dimension bounds of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
papers.abstract: We use linear programming to derive upper bounds for the dimension of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes from local geometric and arithmetic estimates. Rational certificates give the bounds $57$ for finite-volume polytopes, $17$ for compact polytopes, and $15$ for compact arithmetic polytopes. In the finite-volume case, the certificate is a weight function on incidences between vertices and two-dimensional faces. In the compact cases, the inequalities concern squared norms of orthogonal projections of a fixed tangent vector at a vertex farthest from an interior point. We give a common formulation of these linear programs, prove monotonicity in the dimension threshold, and describe the exact verification of the certificates. The local estimates are taken from the companion geometric proofs.

papers.title: Convexification effects of $L_p$-sums
papers.abstract: It is a classical result, quantified by Shapley, Folkman, and Starr, that the Minkowski averages of any compact set asymptotically approach its convex hull in the Hausdorff metric. In this paper, we investigate the analogous convexification phenomenon for the Firey $L_p$-sums of compact sets. First, we establish new structural properties of the $L_p$-sum. Notably, we show that the iterated $L_p$-sum of compact sets whose convex hull contains the origin is eventually starlike. We then study $L_p$-convexification for three classical measures of nonconvexity: Hausdorff metric, volume deficit, and effective standard deviation. For each of these measures, we prove that the $k$-fold $L_p$-sum averages of a compact set $A$ converge to $\text{conv}(0,A)$ when $1<p<\infty$, and to $\text{conv}(A)$ when $p=\infty$. In each case, we show that the convergence to the convex hull is eventually monotone. For the Hausdorff metric and effective standard deviation, we prove sharp upper bounds for the $L_p$-sum of two compact sets.

papers.title: Homotopy types of complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs and applications to right-angled Artin groups
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that, given two finite connected graphs $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$, if the two right-angled Artin groups $A(\Gamma_1)$ and $A(\Gamma_2)$ are quasi-isometric, then the infinite pointed sums $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} \Gamma_1^{\bowtie}$ and $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} \Gamma_2^{\bowtie}$ are homotopy equivalent, where $\Gamma_i^{\bowtie}$ denotes the simplicial complex whose vertex-set is $\Gamma_i$ and whose simplices are given by joins. These invariants are extracted from a study, of independent interest, of the homotopy types of several complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs (such as one-skeleta of CAT(0) cube complexes). For instance, given a quasi-median graph $X$, the \emph{crossing complex} $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is the simplicial complex whose vertices are the hyperplanes (or $\theta$-classes) of $X$ and whose simplices are collections of pairwise transverse hyperplanes. When $X$ has no cut-vertex, we show that $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is homotopy equivalent to the pointed sum of the links of all the vertices in the prism-completion $X^\square$ of $X$.

papers.title: A question of Ulam and a theorem of de Rham
papers.abstract: We generalize de Rham's decomposition theorem to proper metric spaces: every proper metric space has a unique decomposition as the product of a Euclidean space and a finite or countable pointed $\ell^2$-product of nontrivial irreducible non-Euclidean factors. A slightly weaker unique decomposition statement is verified for general complete metric spaces. We use this to resolve a question of Ulam on the uniqueness of square roots of complete metric spaces.

papers.title: Volume difference inequalities for central sections of origin-symmetric convex bodies
papers.abstract: Giannopoulos and Koldobsky \cite{GK} asked whether, for origin-symmetric convex bodies $L\subset K\subset\R^n$, the difference $|K|^{(n-k)/n}-|L|^{(n-k)/n}$ is bounded by $C^k$ times the largest difference of their central section volumes in codimension $k$, with a single absolute constant $C$. We prove that the optimal constant $\gamma_{n,k}$ for fixed $n,k$ satisfies $\gamma_{n,k}\ge c\sqrt{n/k}$ for an absolute $c>0$. For $k=1$, this lower bound grows as $\sqrt n$ with the dimension, giving a negative answer to the question.

papers.title: A sharp polygonal Finsler-Hadwiger inequality
papers.abstract: For every simple $n$-gon of area $A$ with side lengths $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, we prove \[ \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2 \ge 4\tan\frac{\pi}{n}\,A +c_n\sum_{i<j}(a_i-a_j)^2, \qquad c_n=1-\frac{\tan(\pi/n)}{\tan(\pi/(n-1))}, \] with the convention $c_3=1$, so that the case $n=3$ is exactly the Finsler-Hadwiger inequality. The coefficient $c_n$ cannot be improved, and equality holds only for regular polygons. The extremal configurations are far from the regular $n$-gon: the constant is approached by cyclic polygons in which one side shrinks to zero while the others become the sides of a regular $(n-1)$-gon (a doubled segment when $n=3$). The proof combines the classical fact that cyclic polygons maximize area for given side lengths with a two variable minimization using the half central angles. We also compute the larger optimal coefficient for nearly regular polygons, and show that the best constant in the joint stability estimate for side lengths and vertex radii grows like $n^2$.

papers.title: Minkowski problems for $(s,q)$-chord measures
papers.abstract: Motivated by the work of Lutwak--Xi--Yang--Zhang on the chord measures, we introduce the $(s,q)$-chord measures arising from variations of a new family of geometric invariants, called the $(s,q)$-chord integrals. When $s=1$, the $(s,q)$-chord measures recover the chord measures. We study the corresponding Minkowski problems for the \((s,q)\)-chord measure.

papers.title: Sharp Rigidity of Hyperbolic $p$-Barycenters
papers.abstract: We study the hyperbolic $p$-barycenters $C_p$, $0\le p\le\infty$, of $n$ points $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$ in the hyperbolic plane. For $0<p<\infty$, $C_p$ minimizes the sum of the $p$th powers of the hyperbolic cosines of the distances to the points. At the endpoints, $C_0$ minimizes the product of these cosines and $C_\infty$ their maximum. The center map $p\mapsto C_p$ is real analytic at every finite parameter. A point $P$ is the center for every parameter exactly when, at each positive distance from $P$, the unit directions to the points at that distance sum to zero. If the map is nonconstant, the equation $C_p=P$ has at most $n-2$ solutions in $[0,\infty]$ for each $P$, and at most $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ when the points lie on a geodesic. Finite solutions are counted with multiplicity, and the endpoint contributes one if $C_\infty=P$. Each bound is attained in arbitrarily small disks, with prescribed finite parameters and multiplicities, and with or without the endpoint. The proofs use exponential sums over distance shells, a variation-diminishing property of the radial-weight kernel, and the Hobby--Rice theorem. For the upper-half-plane roots of a totally complex real binary form, $C_0$ is Julia's zero and $C_1$ is the hyperbolic zero. Their coincidence forces the center map to be constant in degrees at most six, but counterexamples exist in every even degree at least eight. We obtain the same bounds on the number of distinct parameters for Riemannian $L^q$ centers, the minimizers of $\sum_i d(P,\alpha_i)^q$ on Hadamard manifolds for $1<q<\infty$.

papers.title: A unified approach to logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski inequalities and logarithmic Minkowski problems for geometric functionals
papers.abstract: We establish two general principles for geometric functionals, one for proving logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequalities and the other for solving the associated logarithmic Minkowski problems. For origin-symmetric convex bodies, we prove logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, spectral zeta functions, torsional rigidity, and chord integrals, along with their equality conditions. For each functional, we give the necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of an origin-symmetric solution to the corresponding logarithmic Minkowski problem for even measures and prove uniqueness.

papers.title: Timelike conjugate points in Lorentzian length spaces
papers.abstract: We study notions of conjugate points along timelike geodesics in the synthetic setting of Lorentzian (pre-)length spaces, inspired by earlier work for metric spaces by Shankar--Sormani. After preliminary considerations on convergence of timelike and causal geodesics, we introduce and compare one-sided, symmetric, unreachable and ultimate conjugate points along timelike geodesics. We show that all such notions are compatible with the usual one in the smooth (strongly causal) spacetime setting. As applications, we prove a timelike Rauch comparison theorem, as well as a result closely related to the recently established Lorentzian Cartan--Hadamard theorem by Er\"{o}s--Gieger. In the appendix, we give a detailed treatment of the Fr\'{e}chet distance on the space of non-stopping curves up to reparametrization, a technical tool used throughout the paper.

papers.title: Combinatorial Dvoretzky Theory
papers.abstract: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an $n$-dimensional polytope such that $P \subset B_2^n$. Let $M^*(P)$ denote its mean width, and let $N$ be the number of facets (faces of dimension $n-1$) of $P$. We prove the following two bounds: (1) If $N \leq e^n$, then \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{\log^2(\frac{N}{n})}. \] (2) For arbitrary $N$, \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{n}N^{-\frac{2}{n-1}}. \] In both bounds, $c>0$ is an absolute constant.

papers.title: Support measures in fractal geometry
papers.abstract: We introduce two novel families of geometric functionals-basic contents and support contents-for investigating the fractal properties of compact subsets in Euclidean space. These functionals are derived from the support measures arising in connection with the general Steiner formula due to Hug, Last, and Weil, and offer new tools for extracting geometric information beyond classical fractal dimensions. The basic contents are constructed from the support measures of the set itself, while the support contents arise from those of its parallel sets. Associated scaling exponents characterize the asymptotic behavior of these measures as the resolution parameter tends to zero. We establish a fundamental connection between the maximum of the basic scaling exponents and the outer Minkowski dimension. The proof relies on the novel notion of outer box dimension. Furthermore, we explore how support contents supply aggregated information on geometric features that is provided separately by the basic contents, and how they relate to fractal curvatures and complex dimensions. Our results provide a deeper understanding of which geometric aspects actually contribute to fractal invariants such as the (outer) Minkowski content. We provide some illustrative examples.

papers.title: Polynomial valuations on plane polygons
papers.abstract: Scissors congruence problems involving translations have prompted the study of translation invariant simple valuations. We review this classical theory from a naive and consistent viewpoint: starting from a description of all simple valuations on polygons, we characterize the effect of translation invariance. A description of all polynomial simple valuations is obtained as a bi-product of the adopted approach and as a direct generalization of the translation invariant theory; it appears to be new.

papers.title: Rigid motion invariant valuations on polytopes
papers.abstract: We show that any measurable, translation and $\mathrm{SO}(n)$-invariant valuation on polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a linear combination of the intrinsic volumes, which extends Hadwiger's classical characterization of rigid motion invariant continuous valuations on convex bodies. This result is based on a novel regularity result for translation invariant, measurable, $1$-homogeneous, and simple valuations. As a consequence, we obtain a similar characterization of the Steiner point map on polytopes.
